items.item: Compose an atomic no-replace primitive on Linux, Darwin, and Windows, map the native already-exists re
items.reason: The primitive was already in place: atomicRenameNoClobber calls Kernel.File.Move.exclusive (renameat2 RENAME_NOREPLACE on Linux, renamex_np RENAME_EXCL on Darwin, MoveFileEx without REPLACE_EXISTING on Windows) and maps .exists to the typed destinationExists; there is no check-then-rename left. Added the missing race test: 16 concurrent noClobber atomic writers to one path, exactly one succeeds and its bytes are what remains.

Implemented. Before metadata is applied, the replaced file's xattrs are copied to the temp file via File.System.Metadata.Attributes (on Linux only the user. namespace for .extendedAttributes, and system.posix_acl_* for .acls). A file system without xattr support (ENOTSUP on list) is treated as no attributes. .acls on non-Linux throws the existing platformIncompatible(operation: "acl") when a file is replaced, since Darwin ACLs are not xattrs and there is no ACL API in the ecosystem. Linux/macOS tests: attribute carried with .extendedAttributes, dropped without it.

items.reason: commit() fchmods the temp file to the replaced file's permissions before a replaceExisting rename (noClobber has nothing to replace). New Streaming.Error case metadataPreservationFailed for a failed fchmod. Test (non-Windows): 0600 survives a streaming rewrite.

items.reason: Added File.System.Metadata.Kind.unknown (rawValue 7); makeInfo maps .unknown to it. Tests for rawValue, round-trip and makeInfo with a .unknown Stats.

items.item: `Sources/File System Core/File.System.Delete.swift`: a recursive delete silently skips a child whose
items.reason: Rather than report, the entries are now handled: a name read from a directory is never empty and never holds a separator or NUL, so new internal File.Name.entryComponent builds the component with Path.Component(unchecked:) (exists on POSIX and Windows). Recursive delete, recursive copy and Contents' lstat fallback use it, so names with invalid UTF-8 or control characters are deleted/copied instead of skipped. Linux tests: recursive delete of a dir holding 0xFF and 'a\x01' children; recursive copy of a 0xFF child dir.

items.item: `Sources/File System Core/File.System.Move.swift`: the cross-volume fallback copies with `File.Syste
items.reason: copyAndDelete lstat's the source; a directory is copied with File.System.Copy.recursive (followSymlinks false, so links are recreated as a move should) and removed with a recursive delete. New Move.Error case cleanupDirectory(File.System.Delete.Error). copyAndDelete is now internal so tests drive the fallback directly (a real cross-volume rename can't be staged in the test environment).

api_changes: File.System.Metadata.Kind: new case unknown (rawValue 7); File.System.Stat.info now returns .unknown where it returned .regular
File.System.Write.Atomic: .acls in preservation now throws platformIncompatible on non-Linux when replacing a file (previously ignored); .extendedAttributes now copies attributes
Behaviour: recursive delete/copy no longer skip undecodable entries
